name: Early blight
summary: Target-like brown lesions that climb the plant from the oldest leaves upward during warm, humid spells.
stages: Small dark specks appear on the lowest, oldest leaves.
Specks grow into brown lesions with concentric 'target' rings and yellow halos.
Lesions merge; lower leaves yellow and drop, exposing fruit to sunscald.
Severe defoliation moves up the plant; yield and fruit quality fall sharply.

name: Late blight
summary: An explosive water-mould epidemic of cool, wet weather that can destroy a field within a week.
stages: Pale, water-soaked patches appear on leaf edges after a cool, wet night.
Patches turn dark brown and spread rapidly; white mould forms underneath.
Stems blacken and whole branches collapse.
The plant is destroyed; fruit develop greasy brown rot.
controls: Remove and bag infected plants immediately
Preventive fungicide when risk is high

name: Septoria leaf spot
summary: Dozens of small grey-centred spots that strip leaves from the bottom of the plant.
stages: Tiny water-soaked dots on lower leaves after rain.
Many small round spots with grey centres and dark borders.
Spots cover leaves, which yellow and fall.
Plant loses most foliage; fruit ripen poorly.

name: Bacterial spot
summary: Greasy black spots spread by rain splash, tools and hands; scars fruit and lowers market value.
stages: Small, dark, greasy-looking spots on young leaves.
Spots gain yellow halos and merge along leaf edges.
Leaves look scorched; scabby spots form on fruit.
Heavy leaf drop; fruit unmarketable.

name: Yellow leaf curl virus
summary: A virus carried by whiteflies across the field; infected plants stunt and stop fruiting.
stages: Young leaves begin to cup upward.
Leaf margins turn yellow; new growth is small and crumpled.
Plant becomes bushy and stunted; flowers drop.
Little or no fruit; plant should be removed.

name: Mosaic virus
summary: A highly stable virus spread on hands and tools during pruning; mottles leaves and weakens plants.
stages: Faint light-green mottling on young leaves.
Clear light/dark mosaic pattern; leaves slightly distorted.
Fern-like, narrow leaves; reduced vigour.
Uneven ripening and internal browning of fruit.
